comments.author: @remziyeperkin6911
comments.text:
The phrase "made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs" comes from Star Wars: A New Hope (1977), where Han Solo boasts about the speed of the Millennium Falcon.

A parsec is a unit of distance (not time), equivalent to about 3.26 light-years. Originally, this line seemed like a mistake, as it implied that a faster ship would complete the run in a shorter distance, not time. However, later Star Wars lore explained that the Kessel Run was a smuggling route near a cluster of black holes (the Akkadese Maelstrom). A more advanced ship with superior navigation could take a shorter, more dangerous route, avoiding longer, safer paths.

So, Han Solo wasn't just bragging about speed—he was boasting about the Millennium Falcon’s ability to navigate a risky, efficient path through space.

The 12 Parsec thing has been picked up by a lot of people, but it could have been made to make sense if the Kessel run involved using some type gate, let's say, where you could shorten your distance by using a gate that is not always available, so if your ship is fast enough, it could make all the gates. It could also be that the Kessel run isn't itself a distance but a set of stops on all the planets in the Kessel system. Let's just assume they have improbably fast orbits-- you could shorten the distance traveled if your ship was fast enough to catch all the planets when they're orbitally aligned.
Yeah, it's kinda dumb, but less dumb than what it is now.
